claims.text: A Co-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ni-based high-entropy alloy exhibits superior tribo-corrosion resistance at elevated temperature.
The superior resistance results from formation of a stable, multicomponent passivating oxide film.
The passivating oxide film protects the alloy against both wear and corrosion.
The proposed HEA is polycrystalline with an equiaxed grain structure.
The proposed HEA has a homogeneous elemental distribution.
The intended intervention combines elevated temperature, frictional wear, and a corrosive medium.
The proposed test temperature is above approximately 300 degrees Celsius.
A stable multilayer oxide film forms on the HEA surface under the proposed conditions.
The multilayer oxide film acts as a barrier to mechanical abrasion.
The multilayer oxide film acts as a barrier to corrosive attack.
The complex chemistry of the HEA promotes formation of protective oxide scales.
The protective oxide scales resist disruption by tribological stresses.
Resistance of the oxide scales to tribological disruption reduces material degradation relative to conventional alloys.
The HEA will exhibit significantly lower wear rates than standard structural alloys under the same combined conditions.
The HEA will exhibit significantly lower corrosion losses than standard structural alloys under the same combined conditions.
Superior resistance is limited to temperature ranges and corrosive environments in which the oxide film remains stable.
Departures from oxide-stabilizing temperature and environmental conditions may diminish protection.
Experimental data on long-term HEA tribo-corrosion performance under combined extreme conditions are limited.
The prolonged durability of the protective oxide film is uncertain.
